newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany seeks to change laws on VW rights.
newsitem.headline: Germany seeks to change laws on VW rights.

text.p: The German government has proposed to liberalise laws regarding shareholder rights at carmaker Volkswagen AG, a former state-owned group, a German justice ministry official told a newspaper on Monday.

Rainer Funke, the state secretary for the German justice ministry in Bonn, told the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung in an interview that Bonn would seek to repeal paragraphs two and three of the so-called "VW Laws".
Under current German law, legislation prevents anyone from exercising more than 20 percent of the voting rights in VW shares at the Wolfsburg-based group's annual general meeting.
The state of Lower Saxony, where VW is based, controls 20 percent of VW's voting rights.
In addition, another law scheduled to be changed prevents VW shareholders from turning over their proxy voting rights to a bank, which is a common practice among German shareholders.
Funke said the laws kept the number of shareholders attending VW annual general meetings at about 40 percent of the voting rights.
Funke said Lower Saxony would still play an important role in the dealings of Volkswagen.
"Anyone who has a 20 percent stake is still going to be strong," he told the newspaper.
